title: Short answers: So do I, Neither can I
goal: Reply naturally with “Yes, I do”, “So do I” and “Me neither”
intro: Native speakers rarely answer with just “yes” or repeat the whole sentence. They use a short answer with the helping verb: “Do you like it?” – “Yes, I do.” To agree, they say “So do I” (positive) or “Neither do I” (negative).

rules.rule: Short answer: Yes/No + subject + helping verb.
examples: Are you ready? – Yes, I am.
Did she call? – No, she didn’t.

rules.rule: Agree with a positive: So + helping verb + subject (or “Me too”).
examples: I love tea. – So do I.

rules.rule: Agree with a negative: Neither + helping verb + subject (or “Me neither”).
examples: I can’t swim. – Neither can I.
I didn’t go. – Neither did I.

mistakes.wrong: I don’t like it. – Me too.
mistakes.right: I don’t like it. – Me neither.
mistakes.why: Agreeing with a negative: me neither.

mistakes.wrong: Do you have a pen? – Yes, I have.
mistakes.why: The question uses “do”, so answer with “do”.

mistakes.wrong: I am hungry. – So do I.
mistakes.why: Copy the verb: am → so am I.

mistakes.wrong: She can’t come. – Neither I can.

ex.q: Do you speak Marathi? – Yes, I ___.
I didn’t sleep well. – ___ did I.
I love old songs. – So I do.
ex.fixed: I love old songs. – So do I.
ex.y: Verb before subject: So do I.

ex.q: Is he your brother? – Yes, he does.
ex.fixed: Is he your brother? – Yes, he is.

ex.q: I haven't seen it. – Neither I have.
ex.fixed: I haven't seen it. – Neither have I.

ex.q: Did you like the food? – Yes, I ___.

ex.a: I went to bed late. So did I.

ex.q: Agree with: “I don’t like waking up early.”
ex.y: Negative → Neither do I / Me neither.

talk: Say five things about yourself, some positive and some negative. After each one, add the reply a friend who agrees would give: “I love mangoes. – So do I.”, “I can’t dance. – Neither can I.”
